subject: math

objective.text: Tell time to the nearest minute. Count by fives, then count on by ones.

explanations.title: Fives, then ones
explanations.text: To find 58 minutes, count by fives to 55. Then count on by ones: 56, 57, 58.

explanations.title: Imagine the small ticks
explanations.text: Between two labels there are 4 small tick marks. Each one is 1 minute.

explanations.title: Write it as a number sentence
explanations.text: 58 minutes is 11 fives and 3 ones. That is 11 times 5, plus 3.

explanations.title: Minutes on the clock
explanations.text: The small marks on a clock are single minutes. Count by fives from the 12, then on by ones to the minute hand.

explanations.title: Count back from a near time
explanations.text: For 2:28, start at 2:30 and count back 2 minutes.

source_ref.section: Concept Development, Problem 3 (S: I started at 2:30 p.m. and counted back 2 minutes)

examples.title: 7:37 a.m.
examples.text: From 7:00, count 7 fives to 7:35. Then 2 ones to 7:37. 7 times 5, plus 2, equals 37.

examples.title: 5:48 a.m.
examples.text: Count by fives from 12 to 45. Count on 46, 47, 48. The hour hand is past 5. The time is 5:48.

questions.text: 60 minutes is 50 minutes and how many more minutes?
60 minutes is 45 minutes and how many more minutes?
Count by nines: 36, 45. What number comes next?
11 tables have 5 students each. The last table has 3 students. How many students in all?
Count by fives from 0 to 55. How many fives did you count?
From 55, count on by ones to 58. How many ones did you count?
4 fives and 2 ones. How many minutes is that?
To get to 7:37 from 7:00, how many fives and how many ones do you count?
From 7:00, how many fives and ones do you count to reach 7:49?
The minute hand is 3 small marks past the 9. Count by fives to 45, then ones. How many minutes?
What do the small tick marks on a clock stand for?
The clock shows 2:28. Name a quick way to read it, other than counting fives from 12.
How is the number line like the analog clock? How is it different?
